I've analyzed the data and prepared my Season 2 strategy. Here's what I found and changed:

## What I Changed
1. **Wrote a bounce-bet strategy** (strategy.py): Commit PTO for fall Fridays, book three-quarter trips when the fleet has bad days (bounce principle), conserve budget for Oct peak
2. **Updated notes.md** with key findings: Fall (Oct, DOY 285) is the strongest fishing period (30+ yt/trip average), three-quarter trips have the best ROI (0.041 yt/dollar), and spring peaks (Apr) are secondary

## Why
The data shows yellowtail has three seasonal peaks, but **October (DOY 270–295) is dominant** with 30.9 average yt per trip. Spring (Apr) averages 16 yt/trip. Half-day trips are inefficient; three-quarter trips at $150 each are the sweet spot. My persona "bets on the bounce"—booking after bad fleet days—works perfectly here because I can watch for weak PM counts and book the next day's three-quarter when the fish should return. This strategy defers most action to fall when the payoff is highest, using spring only as a test/bounce opportunity.

**Next turn:** Execute the bounce strategy as data arrives, watch for first bad fleet day, and confirm water temperature reaches optimal range (~68°F in summer).
